title: Cholesterol Levels
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Total cholesterol is the overall amount in the blood, including HDL and LDL. LDL, often called bad cholesterol, is described as the main source of artery blockages. HDL, often called good cholesterol, helps remove LDL from the blood. Triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood.
low: MedlinePlus describes low HDL as under 40 mg/dL in men and under 50 mg/dL in women, and notes a higher HDL may help lower the risk of heart attack or stroke.
high: High LDL can build plaque in the arteries, narrowing or blocking them, which can lead to heart attack, stroke or peripheral artery disease. Diets high in saturated fat, excess weight, smoking, lack of physical activity, stress and too much alcohol can raise cholesterol.
notes: LDL may be calculated from other values or measured directly, and fasting for 9 to 12 hours may be needed. Talk to a provider before making major changes to diet or exercise.
